obligation: Internal report of a suspected incident (all divisions, including acquired firm staff)
citation: N92-R02: CJISSECPOL v6.1 IR-6a (through the Security Addendum sec. 3.01; 28 CFR 20.33(a)(7)); POL-03 4.1
trigger: Any workforce member suspects an incident on any group system, including the acquired firm's VPN, endpoints, and file shares
deadline: Immediately, and no more than 1 hour after discovery
notify: Group SOC (24x7 line); the acquired firm's help desk forwards to the SOC, never handles it
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - one group rule for every division; the acquired firm's 2023 policy (1 business day) is superseded

obligation: Notice to criminal justice agencies (CG-CJ) of a suspected CJI incident
citation: N92-R02: CJISSECPOL v6.1 IR-6b; Security Addendum in each CG-CJ contract; POL-03 4.4
trigger: Suspected incident that may involve CJI or CHRI in the ACMP CJI cluster, its interfaces, or the systems that administer it
deadline: IR-6b sets no separate deadline. Contracts and POL-03 4.4: within 1 hour of discovery, without waiting for the investigation; written fact sheet within 4 hours
notify: Each agency's local agency security officer (LASO), who routes the report to the CSO, SIB Chief or Interface Agency Official, and the FBI CJIS ISO
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all 212 agencies in the CJI cluster (service down); 64 agencies in 4 states with confirmed data theft
notifying_entity: GovTech (group notice desk, group public sector compliance director)

obligation: Notice to the 11 state CJIS Systems Agencies under the message switch interface agreements
citation: Interface agreements with each CSA (contract); N92-R02: CJISSECPOL v6.1 IR-6b
trigger: Suspected compromise of a system connected to a state message switch
deadline: Per each interface agreement; group target: within 1 hour of discovery, at the same time as the LASOs
notify: CJIS Systems Officer (CSO) of each of the 11 CSAs
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all 11 CSAs, because the integration gateway links were suspended

obligation: Agency report of a security violation to the CSO and the FBI (agency duty the group supports)
citation: N92-R02: CJISSECPOL v6.1 Appendix H, Security Addendum sec. 4.01-4.03
trigger: Security violation involving a contractor with CJI access
deadline: The Addendum sets no deadline; follows each state CSA's procedure
notify: Each agency reports to its CSO and the Director, FBI, with the actions taken by the agency and the group. The FBI may suspend access and services until satisfactory assurances are given
applies_at_this_tier: Agency duty for the affected CG-CJ agencies. The group supplies its actions and evidence to each agency on request
notifying_entity: Each criminal justice agency, with group facts

obligation: Notice to revenue agencies (CG-REV) of a possible FTI disclosure
citation: N92-R01: Pub. 1075 sec. 1.8.2; Exhibit 7 I(3) (contract); POL-03 4.4
trigger: Possible improper inspection or disclosure of FTI, including a breach in an FTI tenant, its backups, or its interface
deadline: Immediately. Group target: within 1 hour of discovery, so each agency keeps most of its 24-hour window
notify: Disclosure officer of each revenue agency
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the 2 agencies whose tenants were read and encrypted; the other 5 are told at the same time that their tenants are being checked, because the stolen session could reach every ACMP production account

obligation: TIGTA and IRS Office of Safeguards report of an FTI incident or data breach
trigger: Discovery of a possible improper inspection or disclosure of FTI, including a breach. Do not wait for an internal investigation to confirm FTI was involved
deadline: Immediately, and no later than 24 hours after discovery. The Office of Safeguards data incident report goes at the same time as the TIGTA contact; details follow as known
notify: TIGTA Field Division Special Agent-in-Charge; for network intrusions, TIGTA Electronic Crimes and Intelligence Division; IRS Office of Safeguards (encrypted email titled 'data incident report', no FTI in it)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes. The agencies file. Sec. 1.8.2 also places the TIGTA contact duty on any person who discovers a possible improper disclosure, so the group contacts TIGTA directly in coordination with the agencies and confirms within the 24 hours that each agency has reported
notifying_entity: Each affected revenue agency; the group (TIGTA contact, coordinated)

obligation: Revenue agencies that cannot rule out FTI involvement within 24 hours
trigger: FTI may be involved, but the agency cannot show within 24 hours that it was not
deadline: Report to the Office of Safeguards and TIGTA within the 24 hours
notify: TIGTA and the IRS Office of Safeguards
applies_at_this_tier: Applies to the 5 unaffected revenue agencies unless forensics shows within 24 hours that their tenants, keys, and backups were not touched (shown by hour 20 in this scenario)
notifying_entity: Each of the other 5 revenue agencies, with group evidence

obligation: Media releases about FTI shared with the Office of Safeguards (agency duty)
trigger: Any pending media release about the FTI incident
deadline: Before distribution
notify: IRS Office of Safeguards (draft of the release)
applies_at_this_tier: Agency duty for the 2 affected revenue agencies. The group sends its own draft statements to those agencies first so they can share them

obligation: Revenue agency IRS 45-day notification for the backup vault
trigger: Restoring an FTI tenant from the provider B vault when the agency's notification does not name the vault
deadline: Not an incident clock. Tell the agency before the restore; the agency files an updated notification
notify: Revenue agency disclosure officer
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - one of the 2 affected agencies is among the 2 whose notifications predate the vault (P03 PB-16; POAM-027)

obligation: Florida state agency ransomware report
trigger: Ransomware incident at a state agency, including one in a contractor-hosted system the agency uses
deadline: No later than 12 hours after discovery of the ransomware incident (48 hours for other severity level 3-5 incidents)
notify: Cybersecurity Operations Center and the Cybercrime Office of the Florida Department of Law Enforcement
applies_at_this_tier: Agency duty for the Florida revenue agency and any Florida state-level criminal justice agency in the CJI cluster. The group gives each the required content within 4 hours: facts, most recent backup date and location, whether it was affected and cloud-based, data types, fiscal impact, ransom demand
notifying_entity: Each affected Florida state agency, with group facts
clock_starts: The agency's discovery (in practice, the group's 1-hour notice)

obligation: Florida county and municipality ransomware report
trigger: Ransomware incident affecting a county or municipality
deadline: No later than 12 hours after discovery of the ransomware incident (48 hours for other severity level 3-5 incidents)
notify: Cybersecurity Operations Center, the FDLE Cybercrime Office, and the sheriff with jurisdiction over the local government
applies_at_this_tier: Agency duty for the Florida county and municipal criminal justice agencies in the CJI cluster (most of the 46 Florida CG-CJ agencies; 31 Florida agencies have confirmed data theft). Each sheriff's office decides with its county how 282.3185 reaches it. The group supplies the same content as for state agencies
notifying_entity: Each affected Florida county or municipal agency, with group facts

obligation: Florida local government after-action report
trigger: Remediation of a cybersecurity or ransomware incident at a county or municipality
deadline: Within 1 week after remediation
notify: Florida Digital Service
applies_at_this_tier: Agency duty for the affected Florida local agencies. The group provides the incident summary, resolution, and lessons learned in time
notifying_entity: Each affected Florida local agency, with group input

obligation: Prohibition on ransom payment by Florida agencies
trigger: Ransom demand to a state agency, county, or municipality
deadline: Applies at all times: these customers may not pay or otherwise comply with a ransom demand
notify: Not a notice. Shapes the ransom decision (POL-03 4.8)
applies_at_this_tier: Binds every Florida state, county, and municipal customer. The group will not pay over agency data in a way any agency objects to

obligation: Other states' agency incident reporting laws
citation: State statutes and executive orders in each state where affected agencies operate (not enumerated here)
trigger: Incident affecting a state or local agency's data or systems
deadline: Varies by state
notify: State CIO or CISO, fusion center, or other body named by each state
applies_at_this_tier: Agency duties in the 3 other states with affected CJI agencies and the other affected revenue agency's state. The group public sector compliance director keeps the list in the contract obligations register; counsel confirms each before use
notifying_entity: Each affected agency, with group facts

obligation: Third-party agent breach notice to each affected Florida agency
trigger: Breach of security (unauthorized access of electronic personal information, 501.171(1)(a)) in a system the group maintains for a Florida agency
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, but no later than 10 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe the breach occurred
notify: Each affected Florida agency (the covered entity), with everything it needs for its own notices
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - applies directly to the group as a third-party agent (501.171(1)(h)): the Florida revenue agency and the 31 Florida criminal justice agencies with confirmed data theft
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred

obligation: Service-provider notice duties in other states
citation: State breach notification statutes in each state where affected individuals reside (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI)
trigger: Breach of personal information the group maintains for an agency in another state
deadline: Varies by state (some set a fixed number of days; many say 'immediately' or 'without unreasonable delay')
notify: Each affected agency (the data owner)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the other affected revenue agency and CJI agencies in 3 other states. Apply the law of each state where affected individuals reside

obligation: Agency notice to Florida individuals
trigger: Breach of personal information of Florida residents (for example Social Security numbers in tax and supervision records)
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred; law enforcement may delay in writing (501.171(4)(b))
notify: Each affected Florida resident, by mail or email
applies_at_this_tier: Agency duty (governmental entities are covered entities). The group can send notices on an agency's behalf if the agency asks (501.171(6)(b))

obligation: Agency notice to the Florida Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred (the 15-day good-cause extension applies only to notice to individuals)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs
applies_at_this_tier: Agency duty; expected for the Florida revenue agency and several criminal justice agencies. The group supplies counts of Florida residents per agency

obligation: Agency notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at one time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies
applies_at_this_tier: Agency duty if more than 1,000 are notified

obligation: Agency notices to residents of other states
citation: State breach notification statutes in each state where affected individuals reside
trigger: Affected individuals who live outside Florida (for example taxpayers and supervisees who moved away)
deadline: Varies by state
notify: Residents, and attorneys general or regulators where the state requires it
applies_at_this_tier: Agency duty in each state where affected individuals reside; the group supplies residence data by agency

obligation: Contract incident and outage notices to all ACMP customers
citation: About 1,150 GovTech contracts (incident clocks from 1 hour to 72 hours; service level terms)
trigger: Incident or outage affecting the service, even without data involvement
deadline: Per contract; group practice: status page within 1 hour and every 4 hours while down
notify: Each customer's named contact; status page for agency users
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - constituent services tenants (shared cluster) kept running; CJI and FTI tenants were offline
notifying_entity: GovTech (customer support director; notice desk for security contacts)

obligation: Supply chain incident coordination
citation: Contract (SP 800-53 Moderate IR-6(3)); N92-R02: CJISSECPOL v6.1 IR-6(3)
trigger: Incident involving a cloud or SaaS service in the platform
deadline: No deadline set; as soon as practicable
notify: Provider A security incident channel; the identity SaaS vendor (stolen session)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: DoD cyber incident report
citation: N54-R05: DFARS 252.204-7012(c)(1)(ii) ('rapidly report' means within 72 hours of discovery, 252.204-7012(a)); (c)(2)-(3)
trigger: Discovery of a cyber incident that affects a covered contractor information system or the covered defense information in it
deadline: Within 72 hours of discovery
notify: DoD through https://dibnet.dod.mil, using a DoD-approved medium assurance certificate
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - CUI from 4 DoD programs was on the acquired firm's encrypted and exfiltrated file shares

obligation: Review for evidence of compromise of covered defense information
trigger: Same as the DoD report
deadline: Conducted as part of the report; results in the DIBNet report and updates
notify: DoD (in the report)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - includes the acquired firm's file shares, laptops, VPN, and any group system reached through the directory trust
notifying_entity: IT Consulting with the Group SOC

obligation: Incident report number to the prime contractor (subcontracts)
citation: N54-R05: DFARS 252.204-7012(m)(2)(ii) as flowed down in each subcontract
trigger: The division, as a subcontractor, reports a cyber incident to DoD
deadline: As soon as practicable after reporting to DoD
notify: Prime contractor (or next higher-tier subcontractor)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - for the 2 affected programs where the division is a subcontractor

obligation: Malicious software submitted to the DoD Cyber Crime Center
trigger: Malicious software discovered and isolated in connection with a reported cyber incident
deadline: When isolated, following DC3 or contracting officer instructions. Do not send it to the contracting officer
notify: DoD Cyber Crime Center (DC3)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - ransomware binaries and tools from the acquired estate
notifying_entity: IT Consulting with the Group SOC

obligation: Media preservation and DoD access for forensic analysis
trigger: A cyber incident is discovered
deadline: Preserve images of affected systems and relevant monitoring and packet capture data for at least 90 days from submission of the report; provide access if DoD requests it
notify: DoD on request (contracting officer for damage assessment)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - images of the acquired file servers, VPN, and migration server; SOC packet capture
notifying_entity: IT Consulting with the Group SOC

obligation: Federal civilian contracts (federal contract information)
trigger: Incident on systems holding federal contract information
deadline: FAR 52.204-21 sets safeguarding requirements but no incident reporting deadline. Check each contract for agency-specific clauses
notify: Contracting officers where the contract requires it
applies_at_this_tier: Check - about 140 contracts; affected only if FCI was on the acquired shares (none found by Day 4 in this scenario)

obligation: Covered telecommunications or Kaspersky covered article discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-25(d) and FAR 52.204-23(c); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Covered equipment or a Kaspersky covered article is identified under a federal contract
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification for covered telecommunications equipment or services (52.204-25(d)); within 3 business days for a Kaspersky covered article (52.204-23(c)); further report within 10 business days in both cases. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
notify: Contracting officer (DoD contracts: https://dibnet.dod.mil)
applies_at_this_tier: Applies at this tier (IT Consulting and Grants Management hold federal contracts); not triggered by this incident

obligation: Business associate notice to the 2 Medicaid agencies (IEP)
trigger: Breach of unsecured PHI on the IEP
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery (shorter if the BAA says so)
notify: Each Medicaid agency's privacy officer
applies_at_this_tier: Not triggered - forensics found no access to IEP accounts. Recheck if scope changes
clock_starts: Discovery by any employee or agent (164.410(a)(2))

obligation: Business associate notice to IT Consulting health clients
trigger: Breach of unsecured PHI of any of the 19 public hospital and county health clients
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery (shorter if the BAA says so)
notify: Each client's privacy officer
applies_at_this_tier: Check - the acquired file shares are scanned for client PHI; none found by Day 4 in this scenario
clock_starts: Discovery by any employee or agent

obligation: Medicaid and SNAP applicant data
trigger: Unauthorized access to applicant or household data on the IEP
deadline: The cited rules limit use and disclosure but set no incident deadline for the contractor; contract clocks apply
notify: Each human services agency's information security manager
applies_at_this_tier: Not triggered - IEP not affected

obligation: Driver's Privacy Protection Act
trigger: Unauthorized disclosure of motor vehicle records
deadline: DPPA sets no breach notice duty; contract and state breach laws apply
notify: Each motor vehicle department
applies_at_this_tier: Not triggered - MVSP not affected

obligation: RMS agency notices of a suspected CJI incident
citation: N92-R02: CJISSECPOL v6.1 IR-6b; RMS agency agreements
trigger: Suspected incident that may involve CJI in the RMS or its connectors
deadline: Contract and POL-03 4.4: within 1 hour of discovery
notify: Each RMS agency's LASO
applies_at_this_tier: Not triggered - the SOC confirmed within the first hour that the stolen session's elevation was scoped to ACMP accounts and had no RMS rights. The decision and evidence are recorded; recheck if scope changes
notifying_entity: Government Software Products security and compliance lead

obligation: FedRAMP incident reporting for the Grants Management federal edition
citation: N51-R07: FedRAMP agency authorization terms and the FedRAMP incident communications procedure
trigger: Incident affecting the FedRAMP authorized system
deadline: Per the authorizing agency's terms and the FedRAMP procedure (deadline not restated here; confirm before use)
notify: Authorizing agency and the parties the procedure names
applies_at_this_tier: Not triggered - Grants Management runs in separate accounts with no access from the stolen session
notifying_entity: Government Software Products security and compliance lead

obligation: GovRAMP and SOC 2 customer communications (Civic Suite, RMS)
citation: N92-R08: GovRAMP program terms (not law); SOC 2 commitments in customer contracts
trigger: Incident affecting the Civic Suite or RMS
deadline: Per program terms and customer contracts
notify: GovRAMP; Civic Suite and RMS customers
applies_at_this_tier: Not triggered. Customers who ask receive a statement approved by counsel

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05 (material cybersecurity incident)
trigger: The registrant determines a cybersecurity incident is material
deadline: 4 business days after the materiality determination (delay only on a U.S. Attorney General determination)
notify: SEC (public filing)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Cris Santos Company Holdings is an SEC registrant
clock_starts: Materiality determination, made without unreasonable delay

obligation: SEC Reg S-K Item 106 annual disclosure
trigger: Annual report
deadline: Next Form 10-K
notify: Investors
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - describe risk management and governance; lessons from the incident may inform it

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Any ransom payment is considered
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all U.S. persons. Strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties

obligation: Voluntary report to law enforcement and CISA
trigger: Ransomware or data theft confirmed
deadline: Group target: within 24 hours of declaration, coordinated with the agencies
notify: FBI field office or IC3; CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - recommended; agencies report to their own state bodies

obligation: Cyber insurance claim notice
trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy; call the breach hotline before hiring any response vendor
notify: Carrier breach hotline
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
citation: N92-R07: 6 U.S.C. 681-681g; proposed 6 CFR Part 226 (89 FR 23644)
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after a ransom payment
notify: CISA
applies_at_this_tier: NOT YET REQUIRED: final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; reporting is voluntary until then. Recheck when a final rule is published
